topic: Where the external methodology's functions live in Chohogi
observations: 13 of 15 functions already have a Chohogi owner (routes, execution-allocation, roles, feedback loop, skill-lifecycle) but carry only a fraction of the method
plan authoring and integration closure have no owner
the source's rejection mechanisms were hardcoded artifact paths (docs/<name>/plans, .<name>/sdd, ~/.<name>/) and self-propagating skill-name directives in generated documents
options: A: port as 14 standalone Chohogi-named skills in skills/
B: enrich the owning Chohogi organs and add only plan-authoring.md and task-loop.md contracts
rationale: B keeps one owner per function inside the conductor->route->allocation chain that is always read, adds no parallel discovery surface competing with routes, and follows the constitution's prefer-adapting-existing-asset rule. A would recreate a second skill-dispatch layer beside the conductor, the same competition that produced the original conflict.
reviewTrigger: a naturalized rule is observed being skipped because it is buried in a long route file, or the user asks for name-invocable skills

summary: Mapped all 15 source skills from the read source (v6.4.2) to Chohogi owners: 2 covered (dispatch discipline, session diagnosis), 2 mostly covered (debugging, parallel dispatch), 9 partial, 2 missing (plan authoring, integration closure).

Added task-loop.md and plan-authoring.md; extended execution-allocation (brief rules, post-return integration, model tiers), delivery (test-first rules, completion-claim gate, review reception, integration closure), debugging (one-hypothesis, boundary instrumentation, three-failed-fixes stop), product-decision (design-size classification, per-stage approval, spec self-check), critical-reviewer/implementation-worker roles in TOML and md, Claude/Codex platform maps (isolation detection, Codex V1/V2 source-reported table), homeostasis skill-lifecycle (baseline-failure-first).
Origin (repository, author, MIT, observed v6.4.2) is named only in xylem_provenance/provenance.json; donor naming removed from session-forensics SKILL.md; no active asset names it.

Name-based blocking removed; every function of the external methodology now has a Chohogi owner written in Chohogi vocabulary, with state kept in execution records instead of tool-named folders and no cross-harness skill directives in generated documents.
remainingRisk: The new method text is advisory: no deterministic checker or bounded replay proves sessions follow task-loop, completion-claim, or three-failed-fixes rules.
